title: docs(claude): record serve waitForPort port-race flaky pitfall
why: waitForPort verified only that the port had a listener, not that our own child was the one alive on it; under parallel listen(0) load the ephemeral port got stolen, the child crashed, and start() trusted the thief and returned a dead pid. Prevention: child-process readiness must verify our child is listening, not just that the port answers (cf. the runner.pid isAlive pitfall).

title: fix(serve,server): child-aware readiness kills idempotent-test port race
why:
start() waitForPort only checked that something was listening on the port, not that OUR spawned child was alive. Under parallel node --test, many sibling tests call listen(0), so the ephemeral port findPort just released gets stolen before the detached child binds it; the child crashed on EADDRINUSE (server.js had no listen-error handler) while waitForPort connected to the thief. start() then returned a dead pid, so the next start() saw it dead and restarted instead of reusing (a.pid != b.pid). Flaky only under parallel load; serve.test.js alone stayed stable.

serve.js: waitForPort -> child-aware waitForServer (ready/died/timeout); a lost race (died) re-rolls the port up to START_ATTEMPTS, a live-but-unbound child (timeout) still fails fast with did-not-bind. server.js: handle listen EADDRINUSE with a clean diagnostic + non-zero exit instead of an uncaught crash, which start()'s retry now detects. Tests: deterministic race injection (steal once -> recover; steal always -> give up, never returning a dead pid) plus a CLI bind-failure exit.
